note: Hand-kept, not extracted. The document opens its address section with an outline of which block begins at which address, printed as a figure in the left-hand column of a two-column page. It is a different table from the parameter address map -- two columns rather than seven -- so it is held here rather than merged into it.
why_it_is_here: The parser reads the parameter address map and this is not that table. It is also the half of the page that made the map itself unreadable: on a two-column page the first cell of a line belongs to the other column, so an audit that looks there sees this figure where it means to see the map.
not_yet_joined: Nothing on the site reads this yet, and no unit in the archive is one of these. The document's blocks are broad areas and the archive's regions are what a sweep found; holding one against the other needs a comparison that has not been written, and writing one that merely looks right would be worse than saying so here.
read_as: The page prints one figure per receiving port, each of them two columns wide, and marks the blocks inside it with the group they belong to. The `port` here is the heading the figure sits under and the `group` is the mark printed beside the block, so the two say different things: the same address is a group A block in one figure and a group B block in the other, which is what the figure is there to state.
printed_beside_the_figures: The blocks displayed in gray cannot be accessed in Mode-1 (Single Module mode).
Blocks listed as "#A" are parameter blocks which are common to the entire device in Mode-1, and valid only for Parts A01 - A16 in Mode-2 (Double module mode).
Blocks listed as "#B" are parameter blocks which are common to the entire device in Mode-1, and valid only for Parts B01 - B16 in Mode-2 (Double module mode).
not_resolved: The figure distinguishes some blocks by printing them in gray, and the shading is not in the text the page gives up. Which of these blocks is the gray one is therefore not recorded, and is not guessed at. The two `USER PATCH PART` pairs are printed with the same block number as each other -- 24 and 25 both against BLOCK 01, 26 and 27 both against BLOCK 02 -- and are recorded as printed rather than corrected.
